stream_log.reasoning: Week of 2026-08-31 to 09-07. August's cooling of the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis reversed sharply into the most serious escalation in weeks: a weekend exchange broke a month of relative calm, Iran laid sea mines in Hormuz and fired missiles at a US base in Jordan, the US cleared the lane and struck Iranian targets (Sep 1) while hitting three Iranian oil tankers, Iran fired ballistic missiles at US aircraft carriers near the strait ('calculated escalation') and struck tankers, and Saudi oil tankers were hit. Brent surged ~8% on the week to ~$95. This reverses last week's tentative improvements: middle_east_stability 0.15->0.13 (month of calm broken, carriers directly targeted, Saudi tankers hit), nuclear_risk_level 0.33->0.35 (fresh US strikes, Iranian ballistic missiles at US carriers, mines in Hormuz), and supply_chain_resilience 0.47->0.45 (chokepoint re-disrupted, tanker war, Brent back near cycle highs). global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 1.03->1.02, partially unwinding last week's oil-relief tick as that relief fully reversed - though equities were resilient (S&P 500 +0.09% on the week to ~7,719, buoyed by a strong 162k August jobs print vs 53k expected), so only a small downtick. Russia-Ukraine ran at high intensity - Russia's jet-powered drones (harder to intercept) killed dozens, ~12 killed Sep 1, heavy fighting in Kostiantynivka, and Zelenskyy warned Putin may conscript 300,000+ - lifting cumulative conflict_deaths 1,529,000->1,532,500 (Ukraine front plus the intensified US-Iran/Gulf tanker war). Watched but not scored: the week's biggest positive geopolitical development was the first serious Ukraine peace push in eight months - US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Putin in Moscow (Sep 5, three hours, called 'substantive, constructive, exceptionally candid') then Zelenskyy in Kyiv (Sep 6) with a Trump proposal to end the war, and both sides briefly paused aerial attacks on capitals over the weekend - but it produced no signed ceasefire and the war continued at record tempo, so russia_stability holds at 0.23 (the diplomatic off-ramp and the ongoing grind/conscription plan roughly offset, no decisive single-week mover) and no new node is warranted yet; a signed ceasefire would warrant one. Also excluded: the densest 72 hours of frontier-AI releases of the year (OpenAI GPT-6 Astra - first model to trip a critical-cyber safeguard threshold, Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1, Google Gemini 3.8 Flash + Cyber, Meta Muse Spark 1.3, three shipping gated autonomous-cyber tiers) is a notable capability convergence but consistent with the established incremental cadence and does not warrant another integer ai_development_year_offset tick two months after the 4->5 move, nor a discrete node; Germany's AfD regional-election surge, the Argentina-UK Falklands oil dispute, the Sudan aid-convoy airstrike, and the Dutch central bank relocating gold reserves to London on 'geopolitical unrest' are geopolitically notable but not clean structural movers at meaningful magnitude this week; and the season's major typhoons (Ragasa et al.) fall later in September, outside this window. The Hormuz re-escalation is a development within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis node, not a new discrete event, so no new nodes.

Week of 2026-09-07 to 09-14. The defining event was the sharpest NATO-Russia spillover of the war: on Sep 10 Russia sent ~two dozen drones into Polish airspace during its largest barrage on Ukraine since Sep 7 (593 drones + 50 missiles), Poland and allied jets shot several down and Warsaw halted flights at four airports, and Poland invoked NATO Article 4 (NATO condemned but stopped short of calling it an attack / Article 5); Russia also struck the Poland-Ukraine border area on Sep 13. Combined with Iran again firing ballistic missiles at a US carrier and fresh US strikes in the Gulf, this lifts nuclear_risk_level 0.35->0.37. The 2026 Strait of Hormuz war intensified and widened: US CENTCOM destroyed five IRGC oil tankers, Iran said it attacked ten ships, US aircraft were damaged in a strike on Muwaffaq Salti air base in Jordan, and Houthis seized the Red Sea port of Mokha (second chokepoint re-contested) - Brent crossed $100 for the first time since May on Sep 9 and settled ~$107 on Sep 10 (+~18% on the month). This drives middle_east_stability 0.13->0.12 (war widened to the Red Sea and Jordan; the near-final Iran-Oman shipping-route deal awaiting IMO registration is a partial offset, keeping the slip small), supply_chain_resilience 0.45->0.43 (both Hormuz and Red Sea disrupted, oil at cycle highs), and global_gdp_growth_modifier 1.02->1.01 (a fresh ~$107 oil shock transmits into a growth drag, though equities held near ~7,720 ahead of the Sep 15-16 Fed decision, so only a small tick). Russia-Ukraine ran at record tempo - Ukraine's drone campaign forced an average of ~32 Russian airport closures a day and the Sep 5-8 truce/peace push (Witkoff-Kushner) collapsed without a ceasefire (Zelensky: 'we expect the war will continue') - nudging russia_stability 0.23->0.22; sustained two-front high-intensity combat (record Ukraine barrages, the Gulf tanker war, Red Sea) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,532,500->1,536,500. No new node: the Poland drone incursion, while a serious phase-change in spillover risk, drew Article 4 consultations rather than Article 5 and no NATO-Russia war, so it is scored structurally via nuclear_risk_level and treated as a development within the ongoing Russia-Ukraine and 2026_hormuz_crisis threads, consistent with this log's node discipline (a signed ceasefire or a direct NATO-Russia war would warrant one). Watched but not scored: the Fed's Sep 15-16 decision (even odds hike/hold) falls just outside the window; Super Typhoon Ragasa's Philippines/China landfalls are Sep 22-24 (next window); Copernicus confirmed August was the hottest month on record and the UK banned trade with / sanctioned Israeli West Bank settlements, but neither is a clean structural mover at meaningful magnitude this week; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Sep 10) and GPT Image 2.5 (Sep 8) continued the incremental frontier-AI cadence and do not warrant an ai_development_year_offset tick after the early-September wave already counted; and the Palawan ferry fire and Bangladesh measles outbreak (999 deaths) are regionally acute but not global structural movers.

Week of 2026-09-14 to 09-21. The NATO-Russia spillover that opened with the Sep 10 Poland drone incursion broadened to the Baltics: on Sep 19 three armed Russian MiG-31s violated Estonian airspace near Vaindloo for ~12 minutes (transponders off, no flight plan), NATO scrambled Italian F-35s plus Swedish/Finnish jets, and Estonia invoked NATO Article 4 - the second Article 4 consultation by a NATO member in two weeks. Poland's Tusk told parliament Russia may strike NATO territory 'in a matter of months' and European intelligence services echoed the warning, while in the Gulf Iran again fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and the US destroyed three more Iranian oil tankers (Sep 17-18). This compounding spillover lifts nuclear_risk_level 0.37->0.38 (small tick: still Article 4 consultations, not Article 5 or a NATO-Russia war). On macro, the Fed delivered its first rate hike since 2023 on Sep 16, +25bps to 3.75-4%, explicitly to combat oil-driven inflation (Chair Warsh: inflation 'still too high,' more hikes possible), and equities fell on the decision day (a fifth straight Fed-day decline) with recession odds elevated - monetary tightening into a sustained oil shock is a fresh structural growth drag, so global_gdp_growth_modifier eases 1.01->1.00. Sustained two-front combat (daily Russian strikes on Kyiv/Odesa/Zaporizhzhia with casualties, plus the Gulf tanker war) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,536,500->1,540,000. Held steady: middle_east_stability stays 0.12 and supply_chain_resilience 0.43 - the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed all week (the IEA's 'largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market') and the tanker war continued, but Brent eased modestly off its peak (~$107 Sep 10 to ~$104 Sep 18), so the acute chokepoint stress neither worsened nor resolved, no decisive single-week mover; russia_stability holds at 0.22, the Estonia escalation being external aggression scored via nuclear_risk rather than a fresh internal-stability shock. No new node: the Estonia incursion, like the Poland one, drew Article 4 consultations rather than Article 5 and no NATO-Russia war, so it is scored structurally via nuclear_risk_level and treated as a development within the ongoing Russia-Ukraine thread, consistent with this log's node discipline (a direct NATO-Russia war or a signed ceasefire would warrant one). Watched but not scored: the frontier-AI cadence stayed incremental this week (GPT Image 2.5 variants, Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber uptake) after the early-September flagship wave (GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash) already counted, so no ai_development_year_offset tick; Super Typhoon Ragasa formed Sep 18 but its Philippines/Taiwan/China landfalls fall Sep 22-24 (next window); and the Fed hike, while a genuine macro turning point, is a monetary-policy action scored via the growth modifier rather than an era-defining discrete node.

Week of 2026-09-21 to 09-28. The dominant theme was a diplomatic de-escalation turn against continued fighting. At the UN General Assembly (Sep 22+), Trump said he has a 'big decision' on Iran (a deal after the midterms or 'annihilate'), predicted Russia and Ukraine 'will make a deal,' and on Sep 23 claimed both had agreed to stop striking each other's energy infrastructure - though Zelenskyy said no deal was finalized and both traded fresh energy strikes overnight, and Macron proposed a 'double moratorium' on energy-infrastructure and Black Sea shipping strikes. On the 2026 Strait of Hormuz / Iran war, Iran made its clearest overture since summer: its FM offered to reopen the strait and resume nuclear talks within seven days if the US lifts the blockade, unfreezes assets and ends the war, and Iran and the UAE issued a joint restraint statement at the BRICS summit (highest-profile Iran-UAE meeting since the war began Feb 28). Brent eased from ~$107 to ~$104.5 on the peace hopes (still +~18% on the month). This lifts middle_east_stability 0.12->0.13 (real diplomatic overture and oil easing, kept small because the offer is conditional, the IRGC simultaneously warned it would 'change the geography of the war,' and the Houthis pushed to seize strategic Red Sea heights in Yemen) and eases nuclear_risk_level 0.38->0.37 (Iran offering nuclear talks and a Hormuz reopening, UNGA diplomacy dominant, and no new NATO-Russia airspace violation this week after the Sep 10 Poland and Sep 19 Estonia incursions - only a drone near-miss on Zelenskyy's plane in Norway). On macro, equities hit fresh records in a risk-on, AI-driven week (S&P 500 +1.49% to 7,764.70 and a record Nasdaq close 27,122 on Sep 21; Intel +12%, AMD +10%, Qualcomm +9%; Nvidia's ~$13B Hugging Face acquisition) with the US-China trade truce extended and oil easing, so global_gdp_growth_modifier ticks 1.00->1.01, partially reversing last week's Fed-hike downtick even as the Fed stayed hawkish and oil held ~$104. Sustained two-front combat (daily Russia-Ukraine energy strikes, the Gulf tanker war, Yemen) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,540,000->1,543,500. Excluded/watched: no new node - the Iran overture and the claimed energy truce are unconsummated developments within the existing 2026_hormuz_crisis and 2022_russia_ukraine wars, not signed ceasefires (a consummated deal next week would warrant one); the Nvidia-Hugging Face deal and OpenAI Dev Day (Sep 29) are corporate/incremental and do not warrant an ai_development_year_offset tick weeks after the 4->5 move; supply_chain_resilience holds at 0.43 because the strait did not actually reopen and the Houthis advanced in the Red Sea even as oil eased; russia_stability holds at 0.22 with no fresh discrete internal shock amid the tentative energy-truce diplomacy; and Super Typhoon Ragasa (Luzon/Taiwan/Hong Kong/southern China, ~25+ dead) and Typhoon Dujuan (Japan, 5 dead) were regionally severe but, like prior Asian cyclones, map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude.

Week of 2026-09-28 to 10-05. Last week's UNGA de-escalation turn reversed into a sharp US-Iran military re-hardening: the US ordered a THIRD carrier strike group (USS Theodore Roosevelt) plus ~10,000 sailors and Marines to the Gulf (Oct 1-2), with three carriers to be in theater by end-October; Secretary Rubio demanded Iran's UN delegation leave the US after UNGA talks stalled; Trump said he has a 'big decision' on Iran (a deal after the Nov 3 midterms or 'annihilate') and that Iran is 'ready to fold up'; and an Iranian source said Tehran is 'gearing up for a major round of fighting' (Oct 3), with a tanker struck off Oman. This drives middle_east_stability 0.13->0.12 (the carrier buildup, stalled UNGA diplomacy, delegation expulsion and renewed 'major round of fighting' rhetoric outweigh the narrowing-but-unsigned ceasefire framework and modest oil relief) and lifts nuclear_risk_level 0.37->0.38 (a renewed heavy US-Iran conventional confrontation buildup against a latent-nuclear adversary, scored the way prior US-Iran escalations have been in this log; kept to +0.01 because Iran still has a nuclear-talks offer on the table, the sides reportedly 'largely agree on the steps' to a ceasefire and disagree only on their order, and there was no new NATO-Russia airspace incident this week). Sustained two-front combat (daily Russia-Ukraine energy strikes, the Gulf tanker war, Yemen) lifts cumulative conflict_deaths 1,543,500->1,547,000 on the established ~3,500/week tempo. Held steady: supply_chain_resilience stays 0.43 - the Strait of Hormuz remained closed under the ongoing US naval blockade and a tanker was hit off Oman, but the G7's release of up to 100M barrels of strategic stocks and a modest oil easing (Brent ~$104.5 to ~$101-102, -0.9% to $101.31 on Oct 5) offset, so the acute chokepoint stress neither worsened nor resolved - no decisive single-week mover; global_gdp_growth_modifier holds at 1.01 on a genuinely mixed macro week - a weaker-than-expected US jobs report with unemployment ticking 4.1%->4.2% and mixed/declining large-cap equities (Dow and S&P 500 down, Nasdaq up) pulled one way, while falling Fed October rate-hike odds and the easing oil pulled the other, netting no clean mover; russia_stability holds at 0.22 with the Trump-brokered energy-truce proposal welcomed by the Kremlin ('very good idea') and Zelenskyy ('ready') but unsigned and privately doubted by Trump, and no fresh discrete internal shock. No new node: the third-carrier escalation is a development within the existing 2026 Iran war / Strait of Hormuz campaign, and both the US-Iran ceasefire and the Russia-Ukraine energy truce remain unconsummated proposals, not signed agreements (a consummated ceasefire or truce next week would warrant one), consistent with this log's node discipline. Watched but not scored: a dense but incremental frontier-AI week - OpenAI launched the cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol (1/5 the price of GPT-6 Astra) but SCRAPPED GPT-6.1 Astra over safety/alignment failures, Google released the gated autonomous-cyber Gemini 4 Argon (68% CWE-bench, defenders only), and Anthropic shipped Sonnet 5.5 - does not warrant an ai_development_year_offset tick weeks after the 4->5 move (a price cut and a scrapped flagship are diffusion/pullback, not a frontier leap), and no actual cyber-damage surge accompanied the building autonomous-cyber capability theme (plus the CA AG's Oct 1 subpoena to OpenAI), so global_cyber_damage_annual_b holds at 10.0; and Thailand's floods (2.6M affected, 23 dead) and the ongoing H5N1 poultry spread (US, UK Isle of Lewis Oct 3, Australia) were regionally/sectorally acute but map to no clean global structural dimension at meaningful magnitude this week.
